summary: The change adds a fourth guardrail to the reviewer contract requiring dependency rejections to name a concrete cost, and drops the hardcoded 'three guardrails' count from five live places. All five acceptance criteria are met: guardrail 4 in workflow-AGENTS.md covers ACs 1–4 (specific cost, weigh addable libraries, name the candidate, say what would change the answer), and AC5 is satisfied by amending the already-deployed workflow-AGENTS.md. The count-removal is consistently applied across frame/SKILL.md, review/SKILL.md, and both fireworks_runner.py prompt strings. The guardrail wording avoids the regression the test notes warn about — it constrains how to reject, not whether to accept, and doesn't override guardrail 1. One minor documentation inconsistency in the newly-written story file.

findings.title: Story file Non-goals still says 'three guardrails'
findings.claim: The Non-goals section, newly written in this diff, says 'like the three guardrails beside it' — but the change adds a fourth guardrail and the design sketch's whole rationale is dropping the count. Every deployed file was updated; this newly-authored story file was not.
findings.suggestion: Change to 'the guardrails beside it' (matching the count-free style applied to the deployed files) or 'the four guardrails beside it.'
